title: Defect-cavity narrowband filter with reduced dimensionality optimization
scientific_hypothesis: A 29-layer Ta2O5/SiO2 distributed Bragg reflector with a central SiO2 half-wave defect cavity will achieve transmittance ≥ 0.95 at 1550 nm while suppressing transmittance in 1400-1500 nm and 1600-1700 nm bands, with optimization convergence improved by fixing outer mirror thicknesses to quarter-wave values.
design_principle: Defect cavities in periodic Bragg stacks create localized resonant states within the photonic bandgap. At the defect layer's half-wave optical thickness, constructive interference produces a narrow transmission peak. Quarter-wave mirrors on either side provide high reflectivity in the stopband. This is recalled from standard thin-film filter design practice.
proposed_topology: 29 layers: Ta2O5/SiO2/Ta2O5/SiO2/Ta2O5/SiO2/Ta2O5/SiO2/Ta2O5/SiO2/Ta2O5/SiO2/Ta2O5/SiO2/SiO2(cavity)/SiO2/Ta2O5/SiO2/Ta2O5/SiO2/Ta2O5/SiO2/Ta2O5/SiO2/Ta2O5/SiO2/Ta2O5/SiO2/Ta2O5 on fused silica substrate, air incident
soft_objectives: maximize mean transmittance in 1550-1550 nm band
minimize mean transmittance in 1400-1500 nm band
minimize mean transmittance in 1600-1700 nm band
manufacturing_considerations: outer 12 layers on each side fixed to quarter-wave nominal thickness
free layers bounded to ±25% around quarter-wave initial estimate
L2 regularization penalty on thickness excursions to prevent extreme values
theory_basis: Recalled: Defect cavities in Bragg stacks produce narrow transmission resonances within the stopband
Recalled: Quarter-wave optical thickness (λ/4n) provides maximum reflectivity per layer pair at design wavelength
Recalled: Half-wave optical thickness (λ/2n) at defect layer produces constructive interference for transmission
Recalled: Ta2O5 has higher refractive index than SiO2, providing stronger index contrast for Bragg reflection
Recalled: Normal incidence simplifies design and is typical for LiDAR receiver front-ends
expected_advantages: Reduced optimization dimensionality should improve convergence stability
Fixed outer mirrors maintain stopband performance while cavity tuning sharpens the passband
L2 regularization prevents unmanufacturable thickness values
29 layers stays within the 30-layer manufacturing constraint
known_risks: Ta2O5 name resolution is not in guaranteed_names list - prior iterations compiled successfully but this could fail if registry changes
Exact refractive indices at 1550 nm are recalled approximately: Ta2O5 ~2.1, SiO2 ~1.44 - actual values from dataset may differ
Quarter-wave thickness calculation assumes normal incidence; angle sensitivity not characterized
No literature was consulted to verify optimal pair count or cavity placement strategy
Robustness to thickness variation and wavelength drift is not guaranteed without tolerance analysis
execution_request_english: Optimize a 29-layer planar dielectric filter stack on fused silica substrate with air incidence. Materials are Ta2O5 (Gao) and SiO2 (Lemarchand) in alternating sequence with a central SiO2 (Lemarchand) defect cavity at layer 15. Layers 1-12 and 18-29 are fixed at quarter-wave optical thickness nominal values (Ta2O5 (Gao): 185 nm, SiO2 (Lemarchand): 268 nm at 1550 nm). Layers 13, 14, 15, 16, 17 are free variables with bounds ±25% around nominal quarter-wave values. Maximize mean transmittance at 1550 nm. Minimize mean transmittance in 1400-1500 nm band. Minimize mean transmittance in 1600-1700 nm band. Use coherent smatrix solver at normal incidence. Apply L2 regularization penalty on thickness deviations from nominal.
revision_reason: Reduced decision-space dimensionality by locking outer mirror-pair thicknesses to nominal quarter-wave values, leaving only central cavity and immediate mismatch layers (5 variables) as free. Added ±25% bounds and L2 regularization per feedback directives.
